name: std::indirectly_readable
intro: The concept indirectly_readable is modeled by types that are readable by applying operator*, such as pointers, smart pointers, and input iterators.

sections.title: Semantic requirements
sections.text: Given a value i of type I, I models indirectly_readable only if all concepts it subsumes are modeled and the expression *i is equality-preserving.

sections.title: Equality preservation
sections.text: Expressions declared in requires expressions of the standard library concepts are required to be equality-preserving (except where stated otherwise).

examples.title: Practical example
examples.input: An int pointer iterates over {3, 7} and satisfies indirectly_readable.

summary: The concept indirectly_readable is modeled by types that are readable by applying operator*, such as pointers, smart pointers, and input iterators.
